concrete_findings.title: Interior rejection regressions can pass when all rooms disappear
concrete_findings.observation: The overlapping/nearest-room rejection test and parametrized invalid-boundary rejection test put their result assertions inside `for r in load_interior(scene)`. Neither first asserts the returned room count or identities.
concrete_findings.counterexample: For these inputs, a loader returning [] skips every assertion in those loops. This is a static counterexample to the local assertions, not an executed mutation or a claim that every adapter test would pass.
concrete_findings.claim_at_risk: The tests do not distinguish retaining rooms while refusing ambiguous object assignment from silently dropping the rooms, which can change dataset/geometry evaluation denominators.
concrete_findings.recommendation: Materialize the result, assert the expected room IDs and count for each input, then assert empty object assignments and unresolved reasons.
concrete_findings.qualification: Other cases do assert room cardinality. New correction tests outside the 121-file inventory were excluded; no claim is made about their coverage or current adapter correctness.

concrete_findings.title: Four pipeline failure cases do not assert truthful terminal status
concrete_findings.observation: The parametrized downstream-stop regression covers terminal_failure, dependency_never, timeout, and hash_mismatch. It checks that downstream work stops and that an endstate is truthy, but does not assert its failure/partial status, failure stage/reason, or persisted status content.
concrete_findings.counterexample: A nonempty endstate claiming completion for these failure paths would satisfy the endstate assertion if the existing stop/timing behavior were preserved. This was not executed.
concrete_findings.claim_at_risk: Failure retention and research-run completion claims are not fully guarded by this regression; a stopped failed run could be labeled complete.
concrete_findings.recommendation: Assert the expected terminal status and failure stage/reason per scenario and agreement with any persisted receipt.
concrete_findings.qualification: Separate ambiguous-submission and interrupt tests assert partial status; this finding is limited to the four listed scenarios and does not establish a production reporting defect.

concrete_findings.title: QA legality-summary equality accepts missing metric fields
concrete_findings.observation: The test computes `expected = summarize([score(room, None)])["in_dist"]` and compares `actual` with `{k: expected[k] for k in actual}`. It never asserts the required keys of `actual`.
concrete_findings.counterexample: If the existing `dev/in_dist` summary becomes {}, the comparison is {} == {}. A nonempty subset of the expected metrics can also pass. The preceding constraint-count assertions do not assert these legality-summary fields.
concrete_findings.claim_at_risk: Raw/repaired reference-legality reporting can silently lose metrics while this summary regression remains satisfied.
concrete_findings.recommendation: Assert the documented required key set and expected values, including independently specified geometry examples for critical legality metrics.
concrete_findings.qualification: This is an omission-sensitive assertion defect, not evidence that the present QA implementation emits an empty summary; no mutation or tests were executed.

coverage_limitations.title: Identical synthetic images do not prove correct image-to-identity assignment
coverage_limitations.observation: The fixture uses the same geometry across reference/candidate arms and the fake renderer writes the same flat RGB image for every UID, arm, and view. Hash/provenance assertions can validate records while being unable to distinguish a pixel-preserving permutation of image identities.
coverage_limitations.claim_boundary: These tests support ledger/provenance behavior, not that distinct rendered evidence is paired with the intended room, arm, or view.
coverage_limitations.recommendation: Use distinct deterministic image patterns per UID/arm/view and assert the selected bytes/features match the intended identity.
coverage_limitations.post_audit_version_notice: The visual-pipeline observations apply to frozen SHA f7ef18ffa0974ef81d3090f01e575ad8e202c9f85c8d54be43c6cb7a84a1a577 only. The expected fixture revision has not been read or assessed here; independent patch review owns its coverage.

coverage_limitations.title: Mocked external stages do not substantiate real render/model/metric performance
coverage_limitations.observation: Model libraries and generation are substituted; Blender tests use fake bpy/render output; the pipeline uses synthetic image features and a fake judge. These are useful control-flow and provenance tests.
coverage_limitations.claim_boundary: They provide no direct observation of actual Blender appearance, model memory/context fit, learned image-feature behavior, judge quality, or numeric research performance.
coverage_limitations.recommendation: Keep these tests as offline contracts and require separately scoped, versioned real-backend evidence for those claims. Such work was neither authorized nor performed here.

coverage_limitations.title: Geometric acceptance is relative to an explicit policy
coverage_limitations.observation: Tests intentionally allow support overhang, selected tuck/window collision cases, and inclusive support tolerances. Pose acceptance also calls the production geometric checker.
coverage_limitations.claim_boundary: Passing these contracts does not imply mesh-level collision freedom or physical stability. The policy choices are not reported as defects.
coverage_limitations.recommendation: Name these tolerances/exemptions in geometry claims; any stronger physical claim needs separate independent oracles.

coverage_limitations.title: Captured regressions and synthetic denominators cannot estimate population reliability
coverage_limitations.observation: The adapter fixtures retain 21 historical geometry-error cases; the visual selection case uses a synthetic 1009-case population with mocked backend failures. These are deliberately constructed regression fixtures, not representative outcome samples.
coverage_limitations.claim_boundary: No real-corpus defect prevalence, model quality, success probability, or statistical confidence interval follows from these cases or their counts.
coverage_limitations.recommendation: Use corpus-level sampled measurements with explicit selection and denominator rules for population claims; this report only gives exact deterministic source-read counts.
coverage_limitations.post_audit_version_notice: The visual-pipeline observations apply to frozen SHA f7ef18ffa0974ef81d3090f01e575ad8e202c9f85c8d54be43c6cb7a84a1a577 only. The expected fixture revision has not been read or assessed here; independent patch review owns its coverage.

coverage_limitations.title: Embedded selfcheck wrappers do not constitute a read of embedded source
coverage_limitations.observation: One wrapper invokes seven production modules with runpy, and runtime tests invoke three other modules plus an extracted serve main block. The serve extraction checks for an ast.Assert; the runpy wrappers primarily rely on invoked code to assert.
coverage_limitations.claim_boundary: Full reading of these wrapper files closes their inventory entries only. It does not establish full-source review or substantive assertion coverage of production selfcheck bodies, and no selfchecks were run.
coverage_limitations.recommendation: Track the embedded bodies separately if future source-audit scope includes them; do not count them as extra reviewed files here.
